assumptions: no observed dataset, benchmark, or expert judgment supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
topic scope is learning-to-rank under the ranking_and_relevance subdomain of information_retrieval
single-objective supervised/counterfactual ranking; multi-objective and fairness ranking are out of scope
serving is latency-constrained, motivating cascade and distillation

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable if LTR_PROBLEM_FRAMING plus paradigm nodes resolve

competency_questions.question: How are training instances grouped to prevent cross-query leakage?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable if qid grouping appears in framing/feature nodes

competency_questions.question: When should graded labels be used versus click-derived labels?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable if both label nodes plus conflict axis resolve

competency_questions.question: What query, document, and query-document features and normalization are required?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable if feature plus normalization nodes resolve

competency_questions.question: What loss function corresponds to each paradigm?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable if paradigm nodes describe losses

competency_questions.question: How are training gradients aligned with the evaluation metric?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable if lambda and eval-aligned nodes resolve

competency_questions.question: Which model class (GBDT/LambdaMART/neural) should be selected and why?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable if model-class nodes plus conflict resolve

competency_questions.question: How is ranking quality evaluated offline and aligned to objectives?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: answerable if evaluation plus objective nodes resolve

glossary.definition: Normalized discounted cumulative gain; rank-position-discounted graded-gain metric.
Expected reciprocal rank; cascade-model graded-relevance metric.
Query group identifier binding instances belonging to one query.
Pairwise gradient scaled by the metric change from swapping a pair.
Multiple additive regression trees; a gradient-boosted tree ensemble.
Inverse propensity scoring; reweighting logged data by examination propensity.
Probability a position/document was examined, used to debias clicks.
A non-relevant document the current model scores highly, used as an informative negative.
Multi-stage pipeline of recall then precision re-ranking under latency budgets.
Training a cheaper student to mimic an expensive teacher ranker.
Multi-level relevance judgment (for example 0..4) per query-document pair.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors and domain conventions for learning-to-rank modeling, supporting estimated scores/weights.
grounding_limits: scores are heuristic priors not measurements

nodes.definition: Frame the ranking task as pointwise, pairwise, or listwise supervised learning over query-grouped instances.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: business switches primary metric from nDCG@10 to ERR or adds latency budget

pros.claim: Paradigm choice constrains all downstream loss, label, and evaluation design.
pros.example: Choosing listwise commits to per-query loss aggregation by qid groups.

cons.claim: Premature paradigm lock can mismatch label granularity and metric.
cons.example: Pointwise framing on graded labels ignores per-query normalization needed for nDCG.

failure_modes: paradigm mismatched to available label type
ignoring query grouping (qid) yielding leakage across queries
acceptance_tests: paradigm decision references target metric and label type
every training instance carries a valid qid group key
revisit_triggers: label source switches from graded to click-derived

nodes.definition: Produce multi-level graded relevance judgments per query-document pair for supervised LTR targets.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: agreement drops below threshold or new query intents emerge

pros.claim: Graded labels enable nDCG/ERR-aligned training and gain computation.
pros.example: 5-level labels map to exponential gains 2^rel-1 for DCG.

cons.claim: Manual graded judgments are costly and sparse at tail queries.
cons.example: Pooling depth 10 leaves deep ranks unjudged, biasing recall metrics.

acceptance_tests: gain mapping defined for every label level

nodes.definition: Derive relevance signals from click logs with position-bias awareness for cheap large-scale labels.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ranking UI redesign changes examination pattern or click model misfit detected

pros.claim: Click labels scale cheaply and reflect real user preference.
pros.example: Billions of impressions yield dense labels at near-zero annotation cost.

cons.claim: Clicks encode position and presentation bias, not pure relevance.
cons.example: Top-ranked items get more clicks regardless of true relevance.

failure_modes: uncorrected position bias inflates top-rank labels
acceptance_tests: bias diagnostic compares debiased vs raw label distributions

nodes.definition: Construct query, document, and query-document features as the model input vector for ranking.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: serving-time feature distribution diverges from training distribution

pros.claim: Query-document features (BM25, proximity) carry most ranking signal in tree models.
pros.example: BM25, TF-IDF, and term proximity dominate GBDT split importance.

cons.claim: Feature leakage from labels or future signals corrupts training.
cons.example: Including post-click dwell as a feature leaks the target.

failure_modes: feature drift between train and serve
acceptance_tests: no feature derived from the label or future events

nodes.definition: Apply per-query or global normalization so feature scales are comparable across queries for ranking.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: distribution of candidates-per-query changes materially

pros.claim: Per-query normalization removes cross-query scale dominance, aiding pairwise models.
pros.example: Min-max per qid prevents high-frequency queries from dominating gradients.

cons.claim: Per-query stats are unstable for queries with few candidates.
cons.example: Single-candidate queries make per-query min-max degenerate.

failure_modes: unstable per-query stats for tiny candidate sets
acceptance_tests: normalization handles tiny candidate sets without degeneracy
serve uses frozen training normalization params for global scheme

nodes.definition: Train ranking via regression or ordinal classification on individual query-document relevance targets.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: evaluation shows large pointwise-vs-listwise nDCG gap

pros.claim: Simple regression/ordinal setup reuses standard supervised tooling.
pros.example: Squared-error regression on graded labels trains with any regressor.

cons.claim: Pointwise loss ignores relative order and per-query structure.
cons.example: Optimizing absolute scores does not directly improve rank-based nDCG.

failure_modes: ignoring ordinal structure with plain regression
acceptance_tests: model outputs produce a total order per query

nodes.definition: Learn from ordered document pairs to minimize inversions using RankNet, RankSVM, or RankBoost.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: training pair volume exceeds compute budget or position-weighting need emerges

pros.claim: Pairwise loss directly targets relative order, reducing inversions.
pros.example: RankNet cross-entropy over pairs penalizes mis-ordered documents.

cons.claim: Equal weight on all pairs ignores rank position importance.
cons.example: RankNet treats a top-1 inversion like a rank-100 inversion.

failure_modes: quadratic pair explosion at large candidate sets
acceptance_tests: pair sampling bounds training pairs per query
model reduces measured inversion count on holdout
revisit_triggers: candidate set sizes grow making pair counts intractable

nodes.definition: Optimize a loss over the entire ranked list per query using ListNet, ListMLE, or AdaRank.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: non-smooth list loss fails to track the evaluation metric

pros.claim: List-level loss models full-permutation structure of a query result.
pros.example: ListNet top-one probability loss compares full score distributions.

cons.claim: List losses are often non-smooth proxies to the target metric.
cons.example: ListMLE optimizes likelihood, not nDCG directly.

failure_modes: loss-metric mismatch with target ranking metric
acceptance_tests: list loss reduces target metric on holdout
loss handles variable list lengths per qid

nodes.definition: Use MART/GBDT additive regression trees as the function class for ranking models.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: validation metric plateaus or ensemble inference latency exceeds budget

pros.claim: GBDT handles heterogeneous tabular ranking features without scaling.
pros.example: MART builds additive trees fitting residual gradients robustly.

cons.claim: Tree ensembles need engineered features and resist raw text/embeddings.
cons.example: GBDT cannot consume raw token sequences like a transformer.

revisit_triggers: serving latency budget for ensemble exceeded

nodes.definition: Weight pairwise gradients by metric delta (LambdaRank) to align training with nDCG/ERR.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: target metric or its rank cutoff (k in nDCG@k) changes

pros.claim: Lambda weighting injects rank-position importance absent in plain pairwise loss.
pros.example: Scaling pair gradient by |delta-nDCG| prioritizes top-rank swaps.

cons.claim: Lambda is a heuristic gradient without a closed-form global loss.
cons.example: No explicit convex loss underlies LambdaRank gradients.

acceptance_tests: metric delta uses the deployed evaluation cutoff
lambda magnitudes bounded to prevent blowup

nodes.definition: Combine LambdaRank gradients with MART boosting to train state-of-practice tree ranking models.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: benchmark regression vs prior ensemble or metric cutoff change

pros.claim: LambdaMART unites metric-aligned gradients with strong tree models, a robust baseline.
pros.example: LambdaMART tops many LETOR-style tabular ranking benchmarks.

cons.claim: Inherits LambdaRank's lack of a global loss and GBDT feature dependence.
cons.example: Hard to reason about convergence without an explicit objective.

revisit_triggers: feature set or target metric changes

nodes.definition: Design differentiable or surrogate objectives that approximate nDCG/ERR for direct metric optimization.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: surrogate-vs-metric correlation falls below threshold

pros.claim: Aligning the objective with the metric closes the train-eval gap.
pros.example: SoftRank/ApproxNDCG smooth the rank indicator for gradients.

cons.claim: Smooth surrogates introduce approximation error vs the true metric.
cons.example: ApproxNDCG temperature trades smoothness against fidelity.

failure_modes: surrogate diverges from true metric at extremes
acceptance_tests: surrogate correlates with true metric on holdout above threshold
gain and discount match the evaluation definition

nodes.definition: Train neural rankers (DNN/transformer cross-encoders) end-to-end over text and dense features.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: serving latency budget tightens or distillation/cascade requirement emerges

pros.claim: Neural rankers consume raw text and learn representations beyond hand features.
pros.example: Cross-encoders jointly attend over query and document tokens.

cons.claim: High inference cost and data hunger limit deployment at scale.
cons.example: Cross-encoder scoring of all candidates is too slow for first-stage recall.

failure_modes: latency too high for full-candidate scoring
acceptance_tests: generalization gap within tolerance on holdout

nodes.definition: Model and correct for position/presentation bias during training from logged interactions.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: presentation layout or examination behavior changes

pros.claim: Position-bias correction unbiases click labels toward true relevance.
pros.example: IPS weighting by examination propensity debiases top-rank clicks.

cons.claim: Propensity estimation error injects variance and can over-correct.
cons.example: Low estimated propensities create high-variance IPS weights.

acceptance_tests: propensity estimates validated against intervention or swap experiments

nodes.definition: Train rankers offline from logged data using unbiased counterfactual estimators (IPS/doubly-robust).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logging policy shift or overlap diagnostic failure

pros.claim: Counterfactual estimators give unbiased offline evaluation and training from logs.
pros.example: Doubly-robust estimators combine IPS and a reward model for low bias-variance.

cons.claim: Estimator variance explodes under propensity overlap violations.
cons.example: Near-zero logging propensity yields unstable importance weights.

acceptance_tests: effective sample size and overlap diagnostics pass
off-policy estimate has bounded confidence interval

nodes.definition: Update ranking interactively from live user feedback via online/bandit methods with exploration.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: live metric regression or guardrail breach during exploration

pros.claim: Online learning adapts to non-stationary intent in near real time.
pros.example: Dueling-bandit interleaving updates from live preference signals.

cons.claim: Live exploration risks degrading user experience and is hard to roll back.
cons.example: Aggressive exploration shows users poor results during learning.

nodes.definition: Compose recall-oriented retrieval with precision-oriented re-rankers in a multi-stage cascade.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: end-to-end latency budget or candidate volume changes

pros.claim: Cascading lets cheap recall feed expensive precision re-rankers within latency.
pros.example: BM25 recall top-1000 then LambdaMART/cross-encoder re-rank top-100.

cons.claim: Recall-stage misses cannot be recovered by later precision stages.
cons.example: A relevant doc dropped at stage one is unrecoverable downstream.

acceptance_tests: recall@k of first stage meets target before re-rank

nodes.definition: Distill an expensive teacher ranker into a cheaper student to meet serving latency.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: teacher model is retrained or latency budget changes

pros.claim: Distillation retains most teacher quality at a fraction of inference cost.
pros.example: Ranking distillation transfers cross-encoder order to a fast student.

cons.claim: Student underperforms teacher on tail and rare intents.
cons.example: Distilled student loses teacher accuracy on long-tail queries.

failure_modes: distillation loss mismatched to ranking metric

nodes.definition: Select informative hard negatives to sharpen pairwise/contrastive ranking training.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: ranker is retrained, making prior mined negatives stale

pros.claim: Hard negatives concentrate gradient on confusable documents.
pros.example: Mining high-scoring non-relevant docs as negatives sharpens margins.

cons.claim: Overly hard or false negatives inject label noise.
cons.example: Unlabeled relevant docs mined as negatives corrupt training.

failure_modes: false negatives from unjudged relevant docs
stale negatives from outdated model scores
acceptance_tests: false-negative rate of mined negatives bounded

nodes.definition: Evaluate rankers with offline metrics (nDCG, ERR, MAP) and statistical significance over query sets.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: offline-online metric divergence observed in experiments

pros.claim: Rank-aware metrics with significance tests gate model promotion.
pros.example: nDCG@10 with paired t-test on held-out queries gates releases.

cons.claim: Offline metrics can diverge from online user outcomes.
cons.example: nDCG gains sometimes fail to reproduce as live engagement.

failure_modes: metric cutoff mismatched to product surface
acceptance_tests: metric cutoff matches the deployed surface

nodes.definition: Validate train/serve parity, latency, and rollback safety before a ranking model is promoted.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: serving infrastructure or feature pipeline changes

pros.claim: Parity and rollback gates prevent silent serving-time ranking regressions.
pros.example: Feature-parity diff catches train/serve skew before launch.

cons.claim: Strict gates can slow iteration velocity.
cons.example: Full parity and shadow runs add days to each release.

acceptance_tests: feature parity test passes within tolerance

edges.why_related: Paradigm framing bounds which features and grouping the feature stage builds.
edges.resolution_rule: framing dominates; refit features on framing change

edges.why_related: Framing determines label granularity required for targets.
edges.example: Graded labels needed for nDCG-aligned listwise.

edges.why_related: Framing decides whether click labels are admissible targets.
edges.example: Pointwise can use click rates; listwise needs aggregated signal.

edges.why_related: Normalization operates on engineered feature vectors.
edges.example: Per-query min-max applied after BM25 features exist.

edges.why_related: Pointwise models consume engineered feature vectors.
Pairwise models consume engineered features per qid.
Listwise models consume grouped feature vectors.
Normalized features feed the tree ensemble as configured here.
GBDT requires engineered tabular features.
Lambda gradients require a target-metric definition to compute deltas.
Lambda gradients weight pairwise preference signals.
edges.example: Pair gradient scaled by metric delta.

edges.why_related: LambdaMART uses MART boosting as its tree engine.
LambdaMART consumes lambda gradients as its training signal.
Neural rankers consume text and dense features as inputs.
Bias correction operates on click-derived labels.
Counterfactual training needs validated propensities from bias modeling.
Online learning extends the offline counterfactual policy with live exploration.
Offline evaluation needs graded labels to compute gains.
Evaluation metric must match the framed target metric.
Cascade design depends on the framed ranking objective and surface.
Distillation needs a trained expensive teacher model.
Cascade latency budget drives the need and target for distillation.
edges.example: Re-rank stage budget sets student size.

edges.why_related: Recall stage supplies the candidate pool to mine hard negatives from.
Negative scoring uses the same feature space.
Promotion gating requires offline evaluation results first.
edges.example: Promote only if nDCG passes plus parity.

edges.why_related: Serving validation checks the cascade configuration latency and parity.
Expensive neural scoring conflicts with cascade latency budgets.
edges.example: Cross-encoder too slow to score full recall set.
edges.resolution_rule: cascade latency budget dominates; confine neural to late stage or distill

edges.why_related: Cheap biased click labels conflict with costly clean graded labels.
edges.example: Click scale vs assessor fidelity tradeoff.
edges.resolution_rule: use graded for eval gold; clicks for training scale with bias correction

edges.why_related: Live exploration conflicts with strict pre-promotion validation gates.
edges.resolution_rule: serving safety gate dominates; bound exploration by guardrails

edges.why_related: Pointwise simplicity conflicts with listwise metric alignment.
edges.resolution_rule: listwise/metric-aligned dominates when nDCG is the target

edges.why_related: Aggressive hard-negative mining conflicts with noisy click positives.
edges.resolution_rule: bound false-negative rate; defer to label provenance

edges.why_related: Tree LambdaMART and neural rankers compete for the model-class slot.
edges.resolution_rule: choose by feature type and latency; may distill neural into cascade

edges.why_related: Bias correction changes apparent offline metric values from logs.
Hard negatives change the pairwise margin and model quality.
edges.resolution_rule: control negative quality before pairwise fit

edges.why_related: Distillation changes the model that serving validation must gate.
edges.example: Student must pass parity and latency.

edges.why_related: Label gain mapping should precede surrogate objective design.
Fix evaluation cutoff before computing metric-delta gradients.
Poor metric results trigger feature revision.
edges.example: Low nDCG prompts new proximity features.
edges.resolution_rule: stop when metric delta < 0.01 over two cycles

edges.why_related: Latency/parity failures trigger cascade reconfiguration.
edges.resolution_rule: stop when within budget and parity passes

edges.why_related: Both are non-listwise supervised LTR paradigms.
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct; pairwise adds pair loss

conflict_axes.trigger: label budget too small for graded coverage at required scale
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Use graded labels as evaluation gold; use bias-corrected clicks for training scale.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when bias correction cannot be validated for click labels
conflict_axes.example: Tail queries lack graded judgments forcing click reliance.

conflict_axes.trigger: best model exceeds per-stage latency budget
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Latency budget dominates; confine heavy models to late stages or distill.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when no configuration meets both quality target and latency budget

conflict_axes.trigger: simple pointwise model shows large nDCG gap
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Metric-aligned approach dominates when nDCG/ERR is the promotion gate.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when metric-aligned training cost is infeasible
conflict_axes.example: Pointwise regression underperforms LambdaMART on nDCG@10.

conflict_axes.trigger: choosing a single model class for a given stage
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Tabular engineered features favor GBDT; raw-text/representation needs favor neural; distill neural for serving.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when feature type and latency jointly contradict a single choice
conflict_axes.example: GBDT wins on tabular LETOR features; cross-encoder wins on raw text.

conflict_axes.trigger: low logging propensities create high-variance IPS weights
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Clip/weight-cap to trade small bias for large variance reduction; require overlap diagnostics.
conflict_axes.example: Propensity near zero yields exploding importance weights.

conflict_axes.trigger: online exploration risks live metric regression
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Serving safety gate dominates; bound exploration by guardrails and validated rollback.
conflict_axes.example: Bandit exploration degrades top-1 click rate live.

conflict_axes.trigger: tight latency forces shallow recall depth
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Guarantee first-stage recall@k before optimizing precision; unrecoverable misses dominate.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when recall@k falls below the floor needed for downstream precision
conflict_axes.example: Cutting recall to top-100 drops relevant docs the re-ranker needs.

conflict_axes.trigger: hardest negatives include unjudged relevant documents
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Bound false-negative rate; label provenance dominates aggressive mining.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when false-negative rate of mined negatives exceeds threshold
conflict_axes.example: High-scoring relevant doc mined as a negative corrupts training.

conflict_axes.trigger: offline nDCG gain does not reproduce in live engagement
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: Treat offline metric as a gate, not ground truth; confirm with counterfactual/online evidence.
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: when offline and online directions disagree
conflict_axes.example: nDCG@10 improves offline but CTR drops online.

edge_cases.trigger: instances not grouped by query id
edge_cases.example: Train and test share documents of the same query without a qid split.
edge_cases.detection_method: check qid disjointness between train and eval folds

edge_cases.trigger: feature derived from the label or future event
edge_cases.failure_mode: target leakage yields unrealistic training metric
edge_cases.example: Post-click dwell time used as an input feature.
edge_cases.detection_method: scan feature provenance for post-target signals

edge_cases.trigger: training loss not aligned to the evaluation metric
edge_cases.failure_mode: model optimizes wrong objective, metric stalls
edge_cases.example: ListMLE trained while the promotion gate is nDCG@10.

edge_cases.trigger: click labels used without bias correction
edge_cases.example: Raw clicks treated as unbiased relevance labels.
edge_cases.detection_method: compare debiased vs raw label distribution divergence
monitor effective sample size and max weight

edge_cases.example: Recall@1000 below the required floor before re-rank.
edge_cases.detection_method: measure recall@k of first stage against floor
resolution: increase recall depth or improve recall model

edge_cases.trigger: model inference exceeds stage latency budget
edge_cases.failure_mode: SLA breach or timeout in serving
edge_cases.example: Cross-encoder scoring exceeds the 50ms re-rank budget.
edge_cases.detection_method: benchmark per-stage p99 latency vs budget
resolution: reduce depth, distill, or move model to later stage

edge_cases.trigger: feature parity broken between train and serve
edge_cases.example: Serving computes BM25 with a different tokenizer than training.
edge_cases.detection_method: run feature-parity diff on shadow traffic

edge_cases.trigger: mined hard negative is actually relevant
edge_cases.example: A high-scoring relevant doc sampled as a negative.
edge_cases.detection_method: audit a sample of mined negatives against labels
resolution: raise mining threshold or filter by labels

edge_cases.trigger: computed score field inconsistent with formula
edge_cases.example: final_importance disagrees with node_score_formula beyond tolerance.
edge_cases.detection_method: recompute all derived fields and diff against stored
run DFS cycle detection on dependency edges
resolution: convert the weaker edge to sequence/feedback

edge_cases.trigger: offline metric gain not reproduced online
edge_cases.example: nDCG up offline but CTR down online.
edge_cases.detection_method: compare offline metric delta vs online/counterfactual estimate

workflow.do_first_because: labels gate evaluation and training validity

workflow.do_first_because: primary models depend on aligned objective and features

gold labels gate evaluation and objective gains
gate metric defined early; binds cutoff
high-quality high-cost model needing serving plan

dominance_rules.trigger: irreversible or high-risk ranking change proposed under time pressure
dominance_rules.rule: Risk and irreversibility dominate delivery speed for serving changes.
dominance_rules.required_action: block promotion until risk acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.example: A rush to ship a ranker without rollback is blocked.

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node lacks a satisfied prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: Dependency order dominates raw value ordering.
dominance_rules.required_action: schedule the prerequisite before the dependent node
dominance_rules.example: LambdaMART deferred until GBDT and lambda gradients exist.

dominance_rules.trigger: a numeric score implies certainty beyond evidence
dominance_rules.rule: Evidence label correctness dominates numeric precision.
dominance_rules.required_action: label estimates heuristic and avoid observed claims without data
dominance_rules.example: Heuristic metric kept honest rather than over-precise.

dominance_rules.trigger: a hard lock is requested before acceptance tests pass
dominance_rules.required_action: deny hard lock until acceptance tests and gates pass
dominance_rules.example: Promotion blocked until the parity test passes.

dominance_rules.trigger: risk above threshold or irreversibility high
dominance_rules.rule: Human review dominates automation for irreversible/high-risk steps.
dominance_rules.required_action: route to human review before promotion or online exploration
reject additions that break required structure
dominance_rules.example: No near-duplicate paradigm node added just to inflate count.

dominance_rules.trigger: output formatting tension between validity and richness
dominance_rules.required_action: emit strict JSON and drop prose
dominance_rules.example: Explanations confined to JSON fields only.

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim lacks an eligible source
dominance_rules.required_action: attach SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR or downgrade the claim

dominance_rules.trigger: local optimization reorders steps and risks rework
dominance_rules.example: Features frozen before training to avoid retrain churn.

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient sequencing introduces a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.required_action: convert the weaker edge to sequence/feedback
dominance_rules.example: GBDT<->LambdaMART cycle avoided by a single direction.

dominance_rules.trigger: tight latency tempts cutting recall depth
dominance_rules.rule: First-stage recall floor dominates precision tuning since misses are unrecoverable.
dominance_rules.example: Keep recall@1000 before tuning the re-ranker.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Lock paradigm framing before building features.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Refeaturing after a paradigm change is expensive.
anti_rework_rules.example: Listwise grouping must exist before feature build.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Validate label sources before computing evaluation metrics.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Metrics on bad labels mislead model selection.
anti_rework_rules.example: nDCG computed before the assessor agreement check.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Freeze the feature set before training models.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Define the metric-aligned objective before lambda gradients.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: A wrong gradient target wastes training.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pass offline evaluation before serving preparation.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Optimizing serving for a weak model wastes effort.
anti_rework_rules.example: Distilling a model that fails the offline gate is wasted.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish unbiased offline training before online exploration.
anti_rework_rules.example: A bandit must be warm-started from a vetted policy.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run acceptance tests before any hard lock.
anti_rework_rules.rationale: Locking unverified artifacts forces rollback rework.
anti_rework_rules.example: Promotion hard-lock only after parity and rollback pass.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Require human review before irreversible promotion/online steps.

anti_rework_rules.rule: Resolve dependencies before locking priority order.
